chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Abi Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'It is not allowed to you to take women afterwards, nor that you should change them for other wives, though their beauty be pleasing to you, except what your right hand possesses.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'I see that you are alleging that it is permissible for you whatever was not permissible for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and indeed Allah, the Exalted, permitted His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) to marry from the women whatever he wished.'
He only said 'It is not allowed to you to take women afterwards' after what He prohibited to you, as in His Words: 'Forbidden to you are your mothers and your daughters' up to the end of the verse.'

key_terms.لا يَحِلُّ لَكَ: It is not permissible for you

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'It is not allowed to you to take women afterwards' in Surah Al-Ahzab according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the restriction in Surah Al-Ahzab (33:52) applies specifically to the Prophet after the general prohibitions (like mothers and daughters) were established, confirming his unique privilege to marry more than the four wives limited to others. This interpretation underscores the concept of *khāṣṣiyyah* (special status) of the Prophet, distinguishing his marital permissions from those of the general community. The hadith highlights that while the Prophet had exclusive rights, these were not extended to the Ummah, reinforcing the distinct legal standing of the Ahl al-Bayt and the Prophet.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [33:52] It is not allowed to you to take women afterwards, nor that you should change them for other wives, though their beauty be pleasing to you, except what your right hand possesses, so heasws said: ‘Iasws am seeing that you all are alleging that it is Permissible for you all whatever was Permissible for Rasool-Allahsaww, and Allahazwj the Exalted had Permitted to Hisazwj Rasoolsaww that hesaww could marry from the women whatever hesaww so desired to.

But rather, Heazwj Said [33:52] It is not Permissible for you to take women afterwards which Heazwj Prohibited upon you by Hisazwj Words [4:23] Forbidden to you are your mothers and your daughters and your sisters
– up to the end of the Verse’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from abu Najran from ‘Asem ibn Hamid from abu Basir who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘Other than these women are not lawful or to exchange wives even though their beauty may attract you except what your right hands possess?[33:52]

He (the Imam) said, ‘I see that you think it is lawful for you what is unlawful for the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, when Allah, most High has made lawful for His Messenger, to marry as many as he wanted.

He has said, “other than these ‘woman’” are not lawful for you after that he has made unlawful to you meaning the “women” mentioned in the following verse, “Unlawful to you for marriage are your mothers, daughters . . .” [4:23]’”
